shortDescription: A shop dialog with tabs, money, upgrades with levels, locked items and items to equip, with a list or a grid of items.
description: A shop to spend the money of the player: upgrades with levels, items bought once or again and again, skins to equip, locked items...
- **Shop dialog**: a title, category tabs, the money of the player and a scrolling list (or grid) of items. It works with the mouse, touchscreens (drag to scroll), keyboards and gamepads.
- **Shop item**: one item (icon, title, description, level pips, price button). Used by the shop dialog, or alone.
- **Currency counter**: an amount with an icon, counting up or down (for any HUD too).
How to use the shop dialog:

1. Add the items with the action "Add an item" (identifier, title, description, price, icon, category), or "Add items from a variable" for many items. Other actions give them levels (upgrades), lock them or make them equipable.
2. Give the money of the player with the action "Money" (like "Coins"), and open the shop.
3. Use the condition "An item was bought" (and the expression "Bought item") to apply the item in the game, and save the money (expression "Money") and the items ("Save the items in a variable").
Locked or too expensive items can not be bought ("A purchase failed", with the reason). For real money or a confirmation, use "Confirmed by events" purchases.
Ready-to-use shops are in the asset store [shops pack](https://editor.gdevelop.io/?initial-dialog=asset-store&asset-pack=shops-shops).

events.comment: The item placed in the variant is the model of every item (its position is the one of the first item, its size the size of all the items). The tab and the counter too.
The list mask gives the area where the items are shown (and hides the parts of the items outside of it).
Without tabs, the list takes their place: the original positions are kept.
The size of the variant (the panel is not stretched yet) gives the margins kept when the shop is resized.
In the scene editor, the models stay visible to be placed and styled.
The categories of the property: one tab each.
The events of the scene are told what happened during this frame (an item was bought...).
Clicks and touches on the buttons of the items.
Tabs.
Keyboard and gamepad: arrows to choose an item, Enter, Space or A to buy it, Q/E, Page up/down or the shoulder buttons to change the tab (also left/right in a list).
